title: Rafael and the Detention
premise: Lior Iversen has perfected the art of being unnoticed—until her best friend Rafael vanishes the night of the spring debate final, leaving behind only his car keys and a half-erased whiteboard of accusations against their school's beloved debate coach. Following his trail, Lior uncovers a scheme of rigged competitions and bought scholarships, and realizes Rafael didn't run—he was silenced. As she assembles an unlikely crew of detente-served misfits to expose the truth, Lior must choose between the safe invisibility she's cultivated and the dangerous visibility of speaking up. In the end, she wins the argument she could never win at home—by refusing to have it quietly—and Rafael comes home to a friend who finally stopped counting days.
about_author: Ada Delacroix is the pen name of a former high-school debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers argue beautifully about things that didn't matter and bravely about things that did. She writes from a small coastal town, where she keeps a drawer full of confiscated cheat sheets and unfinished speeches.

chapters.title: The Last Normal Day
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet her counting down to graduation, navigating a home where every conversation is a lost debate, and leaning on Rafael—the one person who makes invisibility feel like friendship. At the debate final, Rafael acts strange, then doesn't come home. The emotional beat: dread blooming under routine, ending on the keys left in her locker.

chapters.title: Detention Economics
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Searching Rafael's locker, she finds the whiteboard photos implicating Coach Merrick in rigged tournaments and stolen scholarships. She reluctantly recruits the school's 'detention regulars'—each with their own grievance—to help. The emotional beat: the first fragile sparks of found family, as mistrust gives way to a shared mission.

chapters.title: What the Winners Owe
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior's POV with Rafael's fragmented texts and voicemails. The crew gathers proof, but Merrick flips the school against them, and Lior's parents demand she stop—her mother's own history with Merrick surfaces, reframing every argument at home. The emotional beat: rising terror and the seduction of backing down, ending with Rafael's location revealed.

chapters.title: Speaking Time
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the district championship, with Rafael found and hiding, Lior takes the podium not to debate the assigned topic but to deliver the evidence—risking expulsion, arrest, and her mother's disappointment. The school board fractures, Merrick falls, and Rafael walks into the auditorium mid-speech. The emotional beat: cathartic climax into hard-won belonging; Lior finally stops counting days and starts counting people.
